Kimi K3.1 Pro review · Barty (5 creative builds, native harnesses)

Kimi K3.1 Pro: Five Builds

Kimi K3.1 Pro (in the Kimi desktop app) vs Claude Opus 5.5 (in the Claude Code desktop app), same prompts, five builds. Each build awards one point each for cheapest, fastest and best output. Host notes K3.1 Pro is the same 2.8T-parameter model as K3 with extra RL training, sitting about three points below Opus 5.5 on the overall intelligence-index table he cites.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RozpfbJ8tfo. Every image is a frame grabbed from that video; click its timestamp to jump there. Figures are as spoken in the video (auto-transcript), not independently re-measured.

Host sentiment
Opus sweeps; Kimi wins only on cost
Opus 5.510 points: fastest and best in all 5
Kimi5 points: cheapest in all 5
  • Consistently unfavorable on quality, favorable on price. Opus won fastest and best on every build; Kimi won cheapest on every build. Final: Opus 10 points, Kimi 5.
  • His recurring complaint is that Kimi's 3D "looks 3D but doesn't function like 3D": doors closing the wrong way yet still blocking passage, a toilet facing the wall, chairs facing out, overlapping truck parts in Blender, an Age of Empires villager walking into the town center. He calls it "a bit of a fake 3D".
  • He also flags low creativity and depth: the boss fight was too easy and visually sparse, the ClickUp clone looked "10% like ClickUp and 100% like every other generic task app".
  • Speed was a real problem: 3 h 15 min vs 56 min on the apartment, 5 h 30 min vs ~1 h on the truck, 2.5 h vs 33 min on ClickUp.
  • Warmest remarks come in the bonus section: the Age of Empires clone (about $5 total) is "probably the best 3D isometric style I've seen from an open model", credited to RL training aimed at 3D work. He suspects office/task-automation work, where K3.1 Pro reportedly jumped most, would suit it better than these domains.

Tests and results

01Test 1Opus (Kimi cheaper)

3D boss fight game ("Iron Bark")

Task

Third-person bow-and-arrow fight against a tree boss that throws rocks; build 1 from a core prompt, build 2 after "make it more entertaining".

Result

Kimi 2 h 8 min, $9.67 total vs Opus 1 h 31 min, $18.54. Kimi's boss died after 5-10 arrows in both versions; v2 added a dodge roll and a new attack but little else. Opus had an intro animation, denser forest, mountains, rock-throw residue, realistic flames, weak spots, and a target-leading boss.

02Test 2Opus (Kimi cheaper)

3D apartment walkthrough

Task

Walkable 3D model of a specific apartment (living room, hallway, bathroom, two bedrooms) with dollhouse view; build 2 adds interactions (pick up and throw dishes, TV, lights, doors).

Result

Kimi 3 h 15 min, $6.60 vs Opus 56 min, $17.17. Kimi: collision works, but chairs face outward, toilet faces the wall, cramped bedrooms, a door closes the wrong way, a door clips into a bed; it did include working light switches. Opus: richer furniture and lighting, correct orientation, breakable dishes with sound, TV screensaver, labeled rooms in dollhouse view.

03Test 3Opus (Kimi cheaper)

Blender pickup truck

Task

Animated truck on a bumpy road, camera passes underneath to show drivetrain and suspension detail.

Result

Kimi 5 h 30 min, 10.4M tokens, $5.58 (only one build possible). Opus 1 h 23 min across two builds, 44M tokens, $23.06 total ($15.51 for build 1; build 2 stopped before rendering). Kimi: low underbody detail, components intersecting, layered tire rubber. Opus: drive shaft, diff, exhaust with welded plates, bolts, no collisions.

04Test 4Opus (Kimi cheaper)

Product launch video (Three.js motion graphics)

Task

Launch video for a lamp, built entirely in Three.js with code-generated sound; no image or video generation.

Result

Kimi 1 h 14 min, 2.4M tokens, $1.25 vs Opus 22 min, 6.2M tokens, $4.34. Kimi: competent, color-shift lamp modes, basic. Opus: coding UI on a laptop, phone lighting up at 11:47, focus timer, more detail. Neither one would sell the lamp, in his words.

05Test 5Opus (Kimi cheaper)

Reverse-engineer ClickUp

Task

Point the "reverse engineer anything" repo at the locally installed ClickUp app and rebuild it.

Result

Kimi 2.5 h, 13.8M tokens, $5.88 vs Opus 33 min, 27M tokens, $14.03. Kimi: functional generic task manager (board, calendar, drag-and-drop) that doesn't resemble ClickUp; sections won't collapse. Opus: collapsible spaces, inline editing, hover-to-open task, ClickUp-like task layout with comments on the right, calendar quick-add. Neither near 60% of ClickUp.

06Bonusn/a

Bonus: Age of Empires II clone (Kimi only)

Task

Two iterations; second asked for graphics closer to AoE2.

Result

25 min / 1.6M tokens / $1.19, then 14 min / 6.6M tokens / $2.68. Host: best 3D isometric style he has seen from an open model, but pathing logic fails (villagers walk into buildings, units stuck behind trees), one bug required a refresh.

07Bonusn/a

Bonus: AI music video (Kimi only)

Task

Generate a soundtrack in code, then a beat-synced motion-graphics video.

Result

Soundtrack: 8 min, under 500k tokens. Video: 2 h 15 min (stuck ~1 h 15 min), 4.2M tokens, $2.23.

Wrap-up

Final scoreboard: Opus 5.5 faster and better on all five builds; Kimi cheaper on all five.
